messages:
jordan: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing a "compact metering" pipeline variant to handle high-cardinality token events while keeping strong auditability. Goal: reduce event payload + storage cost, keep nightly ledgers for exact billing. Thoughts?

sam: sketch the event surface? short schema please.

jordan: sketch below. core idea: emit lightweight per-call token events to Kafka (one event per model-call), keep attribution as compact spans, materialize nightly ledger for billing. Example event:```json
{
  \"event_id\": \"uuid-v4\",
  \"ts\": 1710000000,
  \"request_id\": \"req-abc\",
  \"customer_id\": \"acct_123\",
  \"model\": \"redwood/small-gen\",
  \"variant\": \"q8_0\",
  \"tokens_in\": 42,
  \"tokens_out\": 128,
  \"attribution\": [
    {\"component\": \"prompt_transform\", \"start\": 0, \"end\": 41},
    {\"component\": \"generator\", \"start\": 42, \"end\": 169}
  ],
  \"cost_weight\": 1.0,
  \"route\": \"hosted\"
}
```
Notes: attribution is an array of spans (component + token range). We intentionally don't store per-token text in the hot stream.

lina: big concern: fan-out requests (reranker -> generator -> eval) — attribution must be per-subcall. Need parent_request_id and call_index so we can stitch. Also we need a deterministic policy for how multi-model tokens map to billing.

jordan: agree — schema should include parent_request_id (nullable) and call_index (int). Example: call_index=0 main gen, call_index=1 reranker. Stitching is: group by request_id or parent_request_id and order by call_index.

devin: retries + dedupe question: if clients retry and events replay, how do we avoid double-billing? My take: event_id is idempotency key, aggregator does a de-dup window (sliding TTL, e.g., 24h). also mark duplicate_count metric so billing reconciliation can surface odd spikes.

anita: audit requirements: legal wants per-customer reconciliable ledgers for 7 years, but raw events can be kept hot for 90 days. Proposal: keep compact Kafka topic + cold-object store of raw payloads (gzipped) for 90d, nightly job materializes authoritative ledger into BigQuery and writes compact ledger blobs to long-term storage (s3) for 7y.

sam: how compact is "compact"? can we drop attribution sometimes?

jordan: we propose two tiers: compact_event (always emitted) has token counts + minimal attribution (component spans only). verbose_event emitted only for customers with audit-level retention (enterprise) or on-demand sampling. Compact events cut per-event size by ~6x in profiler tests.

lina: what about reranking where attribution must split tokens across models? we need an "attribution_map" that allows fractional weights per component. e.g., generator consumed 60% of tokens for cost purposes.

jordan: suggest "attribution" entries include optional "weight" (float) default 1.0. Billing rollup uses weight * tokens_out. Also add audit_flags array to note if attribution was approximate.

devin: ops notes: streaming processor should emit metrics: processing_lag, duplicate_rate, attribution_missing_rate, reconciliation_delta. Alerts on duplicate_rate > 0.5% or reconciliation_delta > 0.2%.

anita: add example reconciliation SQL to surface mismatches (draft):```sql
SELECT customer_id, SUM(tokens_in) AS tokens_in, SUM(tokens_out) AS tokens_out
FROM metering_events
WHERE DATE(ts) = '2026-01-01'
  AND NOT (ARRAY_CONTAINS(audit_flags, 'corrupt') OR ARRAY_CONTAINS(audit_flags, 'sparse_attribution'))
GROUP BY customer_id;
```
Use this to diff nightly ledger vs streaming rollup.

sam: storage strategy question: do we need full request payload to debug billing disputes?

jordan: yes but cold. Keep sample payloads for 1% of requests (random sample) and full payloads for requests where customer files a dispute (ingest a request to store). Dispute flow: customer files ticket -> store raw payload permanently for that case.

lina: can we shrink attribution encoding further? maybe RLE on contiguous spans or store counts only + a sparse sample. That would make debugging a bit harder but fine for most cases.

jordan: we benchmarked RLE and counts-only. Counts-only reduces size but loses exact span boundaries. For compact default we keep spans but with 16-bit start/end and component ids to shrink JSON. Also enable gzip on Kafka.

devin: migration concerns: we need a compatibility layer in the aggregator so older components writing full events still work. plan: stream-processor reads both schemas and normalizes into canonical internal record before materialization. Add schema-version field to events.

anita: compliance note: ensure ledger snapshots are signed (HMAC) before storing to long-term. Also keep a per-day manifest with checksums. Auditors love manifests.

lina: question about cost allocation for shared system tokens (system prompts, eval harnesses) — tag customer_id = 'system' and route to internal-cost-bucket. Keep separate ledger entries.

jordan: final ask: move this to an RFC-2 follow-up doc with owners assigned: @devin (pipeline), @jordan (schema + billing logic), @anita (retention + compliance), @lina (attribution policy). I can draft the RFC if folks 👍

arch-bot: RFC updated: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/0002-compact-metering (draft) — follow-up: schedule sync next Tue.

sam: 👍 on owners. small thing: add a field event_version for future migrations.

jordan: added. thanks everyone — I'll open the RFC PR and ping reviewers.
